11.02.additionalInfo: There are seven Jian points, each with a reaction area of the six hollow organs. The five Zang organs store, while the six Fu organs deal with excess and accumulation. Therefore, the Jian points treat conditions of excess in the lungs and intestines, as well as hernias (Shan Qi). 11.01 Da Jian, 11.02 Xiao Jian, and Ce Jian (II) are important points for treating yellow phlegm. Palm Diagnosis The points are located on the second finger, Which represents the lungs, and thus they can treat lung diseases. The three points, 11.01 Da Jian, 11.02 Xiao Jian, and Ce Jian, are located in the area representing the trachea, so they can diagnose and treat disorders of the trachea and throat accompanied by yellow phlegm. the area of the points can also indicate condition of allergic asthma. Shan Qi All seven Jian points treat Shan Qi [fiZ] (hernia). In Chinese medicine, the term Shan Qi has a broader meaning than a hernia. It is related to the leg's Jue Yin and Ren Mai channels. Shan Qi describes a condition of Qi stagnation with pain and swelling, affecting the lower abdomen, groin, and genital organs. These disorders appear more in men due to their anatomical structure. Thus, Shan Qi is especially related to the testicles and scrotum, areas reached by the channels, and disorders such as varicocele, testicular edema, testicular tumors, and undescended testicles. Additionally, symphysiolysis, ureter stones, uterine cysts, and intestinal diseases may fall under this category. Clinical Application & Combinations 1. Treating Urogenital & Lower Jiao Issues (Hernia, Cystitis, Urethritis) The Hernia Protocol: Da Jian, Xiao Jian, Ce Jian, Zhong Jian, and Xia Jian are considered the primary special effect points for treating all types of hernias. Urinary Tract Infections: For cystitis and urethritis, Fu Jian and Wai Jian are usually needled together for optimal results. To double the efficacy, combine them with the leg points Li Bai and Yun Bai. 2. Treating Respiratory & Childhood Illnesses The points on the first segment containing the Lung branch nerve (Xiao Jian, Ce Jian) excel at clearing phlegm (spitting yellow phlegm), opening the chest, and treating pediatric conditions like childhood asthma and pneumonia. Ce Jian is particularly renowned as a special point for laryngitis. 3. Bleeding Techniques & "Miraculous" Effects While needling (0.2 to 0.4 cun) is standard, many of these points respond exceptionally well to bleeding with a three-edged needle. Crucial Diagnostic/ Treatment Sign: When bleeding Fu Jian and Wai Jian, if yellow fluid is pricked out, the clinical effect is considered miraculous ('#12"). Point Name Xiäo ['Js] — Small. Xiäo — Small. Jiän [M] - Small space, interstitial space. Let's examine the names of the seven Jian points together. All seven Jian points have a Reaction area of the six hollow organs. The term 'space' in the point names indicates that these points influence the hollow organs. Unlike the five solid organs, hollow organs have a cavity (space). The names of 11.01 Da Jian and 11.02 Xiao Jian suggest these Jian points influence the intestines. The intestines are composed of two parts: the large intestine, which is the large cavity, and the small intestine, which is the small cavity. 'Da' (big) in the point name 11.01 Da Jian may indicate its influence on the large intestine, called Da Chang. 'Xiao' (small) in the point name 11.02 Xiao Jian may indicate an influence on the small intestine, which is called Xiao Chang. Ce Jian (11), 11.03 Fu Jian, and 11.04 Wai Jian suggest the influence of the Jian points on hernias (Shan Qi). 'Side' in the point name Ce Jian (11) may hint at its ability to treat a hernia that bulges to the side. 'Floating' in the point name 11.03 Fu Jian may hint at the point's ability to treat a hernia that floats outwards to the body's surface, and 'external' in the point name 11.04 Wai Jian also hints at the point's ability to treat a hernia that bulges outwards. 11.05 Zhong Jian, the central cavity, hints at the point's ability to treat the central cavity, Which is the heart cavity. The names of the Jian points describe all their areas of influence.

11.09.additionalInfo: A primary point in Master Tung's acupuncture for treating knee disorders. In Master Tung's acupuncture, many points that affect the heart also influence the knee. The reason for this is that the primary points affecting the heart, such as Tong xin/ling (88) and 88.01-03 Tong guan/shan/tian, pass through the center of the thigh, and if a line is drawn through these points, it will pass through the center of the knee. This reflects an important principle in Master Tung's acupuncture: mutual influence between areas with the same reaction area. In other words, points with the same reaction area can affect areas where points with the same reaction area are located. 11.10.additionalInfo: The points can cause an increase in blood pressure and sometimes dizziness, so the needles should not be left in for too long. Master Tung discovered the points in 1971 when treating Cambodian Prime Minister Lon Nol after he had a stroke. He suffered from hemiplegia, and his legs were cold. Master Tung looked at the back of the hand and saw a blue vein at the tip of the middle finger. He needled a point in the vein area, and immediately afterward, Lon Nol felt a warm sensation from the knee to below the foot. The points increase blood flow to the legs and the brain. The point's name suggests its mechanism according to the Five Phases (Nourishing Cycle): Wood nourishes Fire (Heart) to increase blood flow to the brain and legs. Hu Wen Zhii The points belong to Tung's 72 Absolute Needles and have a unique effect on treating hemiplegia, especially when combined with Ba Guan (11). They can also be used for leg weakness, cold legs, and gout. Li Gou Zheng Vaccaria (Wang Bu Liu Xing) seeds or magnets can be placed on the points and left for a longer time. The traditional extra points Shi Xuan are better for the time of the stroke, while these four points are better after the stroke. The points stimulate the brain, which can be used in diseases caused by brain degeneration, such as dementia. Imaging Imagine the middle finger with the whole body: the first segment represents the lower back, the second segment is the neck and upper back, and the third is the head. The area of the point represents the brain; hence, the point treats stroke. Point Name Mü — Wood. Huö — Fire. Mü [X] — Wood. The points are called Wood and Fire due to their ability to affect the liver and heart, especially in stroke and blood flow to the brain.

11.24.additionalInfo: These are the primary points for treating the female reproductive system. Despite the name of the points, 11.24 Fu Ke can also be used to treat disorders of the male reproductive system. When intending to treat reproductive system disorders, 11.24 Fu Ke is combined with Feng Chao (11) or Huan Chao (11). The points can also be used to treat general hormonal system disorders, such as thyroid disorders. In the Yellow River Diagram, the number five represents the earth (spleen). In palm diagnosis, the thumb also represents the spleen. There are three groups of points on the thumb: 11.24 Fu Ke, 11.25 Zhi Xian, and 11.27 Wu Hu, each consisting of five points symbolizing the connection of the points to the spleen. Palm Diagnosis It is not certain why points located on the thumb are primary points for treating the female reproductive system. It may be explained through the points' connection to the spleen. In palm diagnosis, the thumb represents the spleen, which governs the blood, and blood in Chinese medicine is closely related to the female reproductive system. It is interesting to see that the thumb has three groups of points, each consisting of five points. For treating Menopause and hot flashes, use Sp-9 Ying Ling Quan, 77.19 Di Huang, Shui Ming (one of the 6 points of Liu Shui), 77.21 Ren Huang, 11.24 Fu Ke, 33.04 Huo Chuan, 66.09 Shui Qu. If there is sweating, add 22.08 Wan Shun Yi with Ht-5 Tong Li. Master Tung For vaginal discharge, he needled 11.24 Fu Ke and an additional point between 22.05 Ling Gu and 22.04 Da Bai. Urgent Need for Immediate Results: Pricking with a three-edged needle to express dark, stagnant blood yields immediate, same-day therapeutic effects. Visible/Palpable Signs of Dark Stagnation: Use this technique when you visually identify dark, distended micro-vessels or palpate hard, stagnant nodules along the dorsal thumb midline, indicating congealed toxic blood that is blocking local tissue regeneration. When to Choose Regular Needling Regular shallow acupuncture is utilized for more superficial, generalized, or non-malignant skin barrier breakdowns. General Chronic Ulcers and Sores: For ordinary sores, benign chronic ulcers, or standard open wounds that have failed to close over an extended period and continuously weep clear or standard fluids, regular needling can be especially effective. Boiling Water Burns and Scalds: For skin scalds caused by boiling water where the skin continuously oozes and weeps fluid without stopping, regular needling is explicitly indicated and yields a special effect. Technique and Depth: When needling normally without drawing blood, use a shallow oblique insertion method, threading the needle from bottom to top (proximal to distal) at a depth of 0.1 to 0.2 cun (1 to 2 fen). The mechanism of action of these points can be understood through their reaction area, and the name of the points: "Tiger," in the name suggests their influence on the lungs and their ability to treat external wind invasion. The point's reaction area is the spleen, so they can also treat external damp invasion. Hu Wen Zhi added the kidney reaction area so the points can also treat external cold invasion. 11.27 Wu Hu are systemic points for treating swelling in bones and joints, such as ankle sprains, knee arthritis, heel pain, rheumatoid arthritis, gout, joint deformities, and hip joint cartilage erosion. Lai Jing Xiong Specifies a specific area where the points treat: the fingers and toes. PianJian11.additionalInfo: The point does not appear in Master Tung's original book. Hu Wen Zhi first introduced it. Pian Jian, like Mu Hua (II), innervates the spleen and liver. Both points are located on the second segment, representing the middle burner where the spleen and liver are situated. Mu Hua treats calf cramps, while Pian Jian affects the upper limbs. Point Name Piän [1B] — To deviate, to lean to the opposite side. Jiän [B] - Shoulder. The name of the point suggests its ability to treat shoulder disorders.
